label: Origin-determined access: one world sees another iff their shared individuals have near origins
definition: OriginDeterminesAccess m I means ∀ w v, m.frame.access w v ↔ ∀ x, m.ExistsAt w x → m.ExistsAt v x → I.near (I.origin w x) (I.origin v x). The same x is compared at both worlds, using rigid identity in Ontic. The access-to-closeness direction constrains the origins of every shared individual; the closeness-to-access direction additionally says that no other restriction blocks access. Worlds sharing no individual are accessible by the vacuity of the shared-individual condition. Neither direction requires an individual to exist at another world.
note: Open analyst framework commitment, attribution deferred. Dependencies: 622524e2-e7f3-4b27-a644-bf9a4235121b, DEF-KANT-ONTOLOGICAL-MODEL and DEF-MODAL-FIXTURE-FRAME. The biconditional is an explicit premise, not a settled definition of metaphysical possibility. Its sufficiency direction is distinct from OriginPlenitude, which supplies worlds with a chosen near origin, and from individual or joint deletion. The five-world Control.faithful supplies the stipulated example; Control.restored satisfies the same criterion but has a necessary individual. Counterpart matching, literal equality of worlds or origins, causal explanation and temporal succession are not this relation. In Control.faithful, access fails exactly between aMinus and plus and between bMinus and bPlus. An access relation that additionally forbids a pair satisfying shared-origin closeness can satisfy the only-if half while failing the if half, for example when a separate nomological or recombination constraint forbids that pair. Deletion of an individual from an accessible world is neither required nor excluded by this criterion. The earlier NecessaryIf link defines box(G -> box G), not origin vocabulary.
